statement: A real or complex sequence is a function whose domain is an integer index set such as the positive integers; its analytic content concerns the behavior of the indexed values as the index grows.
scope_limits: Uses the generic function concept already owned by C01/C03; this claim specializes it to sequences in analysis.

statement: A sequence (a_n) converges to L exactly when for every epsilon>0 there exists N such that n>=N implies |a_n-L|<epsilon.
scope_limits: Sequence limits only; function continuity is owned by T02.

statement: A convergent sequence has a unique limit.
scope_limits: Real/complex sequences in the standard metric.

statement: Every convergent real or complex sequence is bounded.
scope_limits: The converse is false without additional hypotheses.

statement: Finite algebraic combinations of convergent real or complex sequences have the corresponding algebraic limits whenever every invoked operation is defined, including quotients whose limiting denominator is nonzero.
scope_limits: Scalar limit laws; does not re-author C02 arithmetic laws.

statement: Every monotone bounded real sequence converges.
scope_limits: Uses completeness/order properties of the real numbers already owned by C02.

statement: A real sequence converges if and only if it is a Cauchy sequence.
scope_limits: Analytic consequence of completeness of R; C02 retains ownership of the real-number system itself.

statement: Every bounded real sequence has a convergent subsequence.
scope_limits: Bolzano–Weierstrass for real sequences; generic topology remains outside C05 ownership.

statement: A function f is continuous at a point a in its domain exactly when for every epsilon>0 there exists delta>0 such that domain points x with |x-a|<delta satisfy |f(x)-f(a)|<epsilon.
scope_limits: Real/complex metric setting used for analysis; generic function identity remains C01/C03 ownership.

statement: For real or complex functions on metric subspaces, continuity at a is equivalent to f(x_n)→f(a) for every sequence x_n→a with x_n in the domain.
scope_limits: Uses T01 sequence convergence as a criterion; it does not transfer T01 ownership.

statement: The composition of functions continuous at the relevant points is continuous at the composed point.
scope_limits: Composition as an algebraic operation is inherited from C03; this claim owns its continuity consequence.

statement: Sums and products of continuous scalar-valued functions are continuous, and quotients are continuous wherever the denominator is nonzero.
scope_limits: Continuity preservation only; scalar arithmetic itself remains C02 ownership.

statement: If a real-valued function is continuous on [a,b], then it assumes every value between f(a) and f(b).
scope_limits: Intermediate Value Theorem on a closed interval.

statement: A real-valued function continuous on a closed bounded interval attains both a maximum and a minimum there.
scope_limits: Extreme Value Theorem in one-dimensional real analysis; generic compactness ownership is not transferred from future C09.

statement: A function is uniformly continuous on a set when one delta can be chosen for each epsilon independently of the particular pair of points in that set.
scope_limits: Analysis-specific uniform continuity definition.

statement: Every continuous function on a closed bounded real interval is uniformly continuous there.
scope_limits: Heine–Cantor in the interval setting; C09 generic topology remains locked.

statement: The derivative f'(a) is the limit of [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h as h→0 when that finite limit exists.
scope_limits: One-variable derivative only; multivariable derivative belongs to T06.

statement: Differentiability of a one-variable function at a point implies continuity at that point.
scope_limits: The converse need not hold.

statement: If f is differentiable at a, then f(a+h)=f(a)+f'(a)h+r(h) with r(h)/h→0 as h→0, so the derivative gives the first-order linear approximation in one variable.
scope_limits: Analytic linear approximation; geometric tangent interpretation is boundary/example only and remains C04 ownership.

statement: Differentiable functions satisfy the linearity, product, and quotient differentiation rules wherever the quotient denominator is nonzero.
scope_limits: Standard one-variable differentiation rules.

statement: If f is differentiable at a and g is differentiable at f(a), then g∘f is differentiable at a with derivative g'(f(a))f'(a).
scope_limits: One-variable chain rule; T06 owns the multivariable linear-map form.

statement: If f has a local extremum at an interior point c and is differentiable at c, then f'(c)=0.
scope_limits: Necessary condition at an interior differentiable local extremum; not a sufficient condition for extremality.

statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), then some c in (a,b) satisfies f'(c)=[f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a).
scope_limits: Mean Value Theorem with its standard hypotheses.

statement: Under the standard differentiability hypotheses, Taylor's theorem represents a function by a finite Taylor polynomial plus a remainder whose form or bound records the approximation error.
scope_limits: Finite-order one-variable Taylor theorem; convergence of an infinite Taylor series is a separate question.

statement: A bounded function on [a,b] is Riemann integrable when its tagged Riemann sums approach one common finite limit as the partition mesh tends to zero, equivalently under standard Riemann/Darboux criteria.
scope_limits: Riemann integration only; Lebesgue integration is T07 ownership.

statement: Every real-valued continuous function on a closed bounded interval is Riemann integrable.
scope_limits: One-variable Riemann theorem on compact intervals.

statement: The Riemann integral is linear: the integral of alpha f+beta g equals alpha times the integral of f plus beta times the integral of g for Riemann-integrable f and g.
scope_limits: Finite scalar linearity of the Riemann integral.

statement: For an integrable function and a point c between a and b, the integral over [a,b] equals the sum of the integrals over [a,c] and [c,b].
scope_limits: Interval additivity of the Riemann integral.

statement: If f and g are Riemann integrable on [a,b] and f(x)<=g(x) throughout the interval, then the integral of f is at most the integral of g.
scope_limits: Order preservation of the Riemann integral; ordered scalar primitives remain C02 ownership.

statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and F(x)=∫_a^x f(t)dt, then F is differentiable on (a,b) and F'(x)=f(x).
scope_limits: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, accumulation-to-derivative direction.

statement: If F is an antiderivative of a continuous f on [a,b], then ∫_a^b f(x)dx=F(b)-F(a).
scope_limits: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, evaluation direction.

statement: A differentiable change of variable with the usual continuity and domain hypotheses transforms an integral according to the substitution rule by multiplying with the derivative of the change of variable.
scope_limits: One-variable substitution theorem; exact hypotheses must be checked in use.

statement: An improper integral over an unbounded interval or near a singular endpoint is defined through a limit of proper integrals and converges only when the defining finite limit exists.
scope_limits: Elementary improper Riemann integration; measure-theoretic integration belongs to T07.

statement: For continuously differentiable functions u and v, integration by parts satisfies ∫_a^b u(x)v'(x)dx=[u(x)v(x)]_a^b-∫_a^b u'(x)v(x)dx.
scope_limits: One-variable integration-by-parts identity derived from the product rule and FTC.

statement: An infinite series ∑a_n converges exactly when its sequence of partial sums converges to a finite limit, and the value of the series is that limit.
scope_limits: T05 specializes T01 sequence convergence to partial sums.

statement: The geometric series ∑_{n=0}^∞ r^n converges to 1/(1-r) when |r|<1 and diverges when |r|>=1.
scope_limits: Scalar geometric series.

statement: If ∑a_n converges, then a_n→0; the condition a_n→0 alone is not sufficient for convergence of the series.
scope_limits: Necessary term test together with its non-converse.

statement: Absolute convergence of a scalar series implies convergence of the series.
scope_limits: Real/complex scalar series.

statement: For nonnegative series, domination by a convergent comparison series implies convergence, while domination of a known divergent series by the tested terms gives divergence in the corresponding comparison direction.
scope_limits: Direct comparison principle for nonnegative terms.

statement: When the limit L=lim |a_{n+1}/a_n| exists, the ratio test gives absolute convergence for L<1 and divergence for L>1; L=1 is inconclusive.
scope_limits: Ratio test under existence of the stated limit.

statement: When the limit L=lim |a_n|^(1/n) exists, the root test gives absolute convergence for L<1 and divergence for L>1; L=1 is inconclusive.
scope_limits: Root test under existence of the stated limit.

statement: If a nonincreasing sequence b_n of nonnegative numbers tends to zero, then the alternating series ∑(-1)^n b_n converges.
scope_limits: Alternating-series criterion; absolute convergence is not implied.

statement: Every power series ∑c_n(x-a)^n has a radius R in [0,∞] such that it converges absolutely for |x-a|<R and diverges for |x-a|>R, while boundary points require separate analysis.
scope_limits: Generic power-series convergence; Fourier series and Fourier coefficients belong to T10.
